(2) SNGPL's 'Province-Wise Transmission Breakup' table (live HTML, page heading 'Province-Wise Breakup Transmission System as on 30-06-2025'; url_verifier confirms HTTP 200 with 'SHAHDARA'/'FAISALABAD' literally present) contains, under Section='FSD - SHAHDARA' (FSD = Faisalabad, the same abbreviation confirmed on the sibling row P4128's exact-match 'FSD - MALIKWAL'=158.67km): Sr#95 dia=16in, MainLine=57.48km, LoopLine=119.25km; Sr#97 dia=24in, MainLine=55.03km, no loop. 119.25 km is an EXACT match to sibling row P4135's (Faisalabad-Shahdara Gas Pipeline-I) recorded length+diameter (16in) -- it is the corridor's LoopLine. And 57.48 + 55.03 = 112.51 km EXACTLY equals P4136's recorded LengthKnown, while the two diameters summed (16in segment + 24in segment) exactly match P4136's recorded dual-diameter field '16, 24' -- P4136 is the corridor's two MainLine sub-segments (16in for 57.48km, transitioning to 24in for 55.03km), not a duplicate of P4135's loopline. This is a striking, essentially non-coincidental numeric match (agreement to the hundredth of a km on a derived sum) that confirms GEM's researcher pulled this row directly from an earlier vintage of this exact SNGPL table -- legitimate sourcing that was simply never captured as a citable [ref], not fabrication. Status=operating is confirmed by the map's 'Existing Pipeline' legend (solid red, distinct from a would-be planned/dashed style) and by inclusion in the CURRENT (30-06-2025) breakup table. Owner=SNGPL is confirmed trivially -- this is literally SNGPL's own published transmission-system map/table of its own assets. Duplicate check against the 63-row roster: P4135 (Phase I, 16in, 119.25km) and P4136 (Phase II, dual 16/24in, 112.51km) are NOT a duplicate pair -- they are two genuinely distinct physical pipes on the same corridor (SNGPL's own MainLine vs LoopLine columns), consistent with GEM's established convention elsewhere on this exact roster for multi-loop corridors (Sui-Multan I/II/III, Sidhnai-Faisalabad I/II, Sahiwal-Lahore I/II, Dandot-Gali Jagir-Wah I/II).
